title: Knowledge-graph machine learning nominates niclosamide and tribromsalan for mycobacteria
summary: A semantic knowledge-graph approach combined with machine-learning models nominated known molecules for anti-mycobacterial testing. Niclosamide inhibited Mycobacterium tuberculosis (IC90 2.95 uM) and M. abscessus (IC90 59.1 uM), and tribromsalan inhibited them at IC90 76.92 and 147.4 uM, in vitro. Transcriptional profiling showed respiratory-pathway stress and altered fatty-acid metabolism, differing from known M. tuberculosis inhibitors; the compounds are repurposed drugs tested only in vitro.
ai_technology: Semantic knowledge graph with machine-learning models for drug-disease association
organization: University of New Mexico; Indiana University Bloomington; Indiana University

evidence.tested: In vitro IC90 testing against M. tuberculosis and M. abscessus plus transcriptional response profiling.
evidence.unknown: In vivo efficacy and clinical relevance of the repurposed compounds; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Knowledge-graph and machine-learning models nominated repositioning candidates.
